Recently, Bruinier and Ono classified cusp forms $f(z) := \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_f(n)q ^n \in S_{\lambda+1/2}(\Gamma_0(N),\chi)\cap \mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ that does not satisfy a certain distribution property for modulo odd primes $p$. In this paper, using Rankin-Cohen Bracket, we extend this result to modular forms of half integral weight for primes $p \geq 5$. As applications of our main theorem we derive distribution properties, for modulo primes $p\geq5$, of traces of singular moduli and Hurwitz class number. We also study an analogue of Newman's conjecture for overpartitions.

Bruinier and Ono previously classified certain cusp forms of half-integral weight with integer coefficients that fail to satisfy a particular distribution property modulo odd primes. Their work identified exceptional cases in which the Fourier coefficients of such modular forms do not distribute as expected in residue classes modulo a prime.

The present paper extends this classification from half-integral weight cusp forms to a broader class of modular forms of half-integral weight, focusing on primes \(p \geq 5\). A key tool in this extension is the Rankin-Cohen bracket, which allows the authors to relate half-integral weight modular forms to cusp forms in a way that makes it possible to apply and generalize earlier classification results. Through this method, the paper establishes a main theorem describing when such modular forms fail to have the desired coefficient distribution property modulo primes \(p \geq 5\).

The authors then apply their main theorem to the arithmetic of traces of singular moduli. These traces arise naturally in the theory of modular functions and complex multiplication, and they are encoded in the Fourier coefficients of certain half-integral weight modular forms. Using the extended classification, the paper proves distribution results modulo primes \(p \geq 5\) for these traces, showing that they satisfy the expected distribution properties except in precisely controlled exceptional situations.

A further application concerns Hurwitz class numbers, which count equivalence classes of positive definite binary quadratic forms with prescribed discriminant, with appropriate weights for automorphisms. Since Hurwitz class numbers also appear as coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms, the authors are able to use their main theorem to establish analogous distribution properties modulo primes \(p \geq 5\). These results give information about how class numbers behave in residue classes modulo such primes.

Finally, the paper studies an analogue of Newman’s conjecture for overpartitions. Overpartitions are partition-theoretic objects in which the first occurrence of each distinct part may be overlined. Newman’s conjecture concerns the distribution of partition functions modulo primes, and the authors investigate a corresponding question for the overpartition function. By connecting overpartition generating functions with half-integral weight modular forms, they analyze when the coefficients are well distributed modulo primes and identify the relevant exceptional cases.

Bruinier and Ono classified certain half-integral weight cusp forms whose Fourier coefficients fail to satisfy expected distribution properties modulo a prime. The present work extends this classification beyond the original setting by applying Rankin–Cohen brackets, which allow one to relate more general half-integral weight modular forms to cusp forms of suitable weights. In this way, the authors obtain a broader theorem for modular forms of half-integral weight modulo primes \(p \ge 5\), describing when their Fourier coefficients are well distributed modulo \(p\) and identifying the exceptional cases.

A central feature of the paper is the use of this main theorem to study arithmetic sequences arising from classical objects in the theory of modular forms. In particular, the authors apply their results to traces of singular moduli and to Hurwitz class numbers. These quantities occur as Fourier coefficients of modular or mock modular forms of half-integral weight, and the new distribution theorem provides congruence information about their values modulo primes. As a result, the paper establishes that, outside explicitly described exceptional situations, these arithmetic functions attain residue classes modulo \(p\) with the expected frequency or at least with strong nonvanishing and distribution behavior.

The paper also explores applications beyond the classical theory of class numbers and singular moduli. One such application concerns overpartitions, a variant of integer partitions in which the first occurrence of a part may be overlined. Motivated by Newman’s conjecture on the distribution of the ordinary partition function modulo primes, the authors investigate an analogous question for the overpartition function. Using the modular-form techniques developed earlier in the paper, they obtain evidence and results showing that overpartition values exhibit comparable modulo-prime distribution phenomena.

Overall, the work demonstrates the effectiveness of Rankin–Cohen brackets as a tool for transferring distribution results from cusp forms to more general half-integral weight modular forms. It extends the reach of Bruinier and Ono’s classification, proves new congruence and distribution theorems for important arithmetic sequences such as traces of singular moduli and Hurwitz class numbers, and connects these ideas to partition-theoretic questions inspired by Newman’s conjecture. The paper therefore illustrates the broad arithmetic significance of half-integral weight modular forms and their Fourier coefficients modulo primes.

Recently, Bruinier and Ono made important contributions to the study of integer partitions, modular forms, and number theory. Their work is especially notable because it connects the partition function, one of the most classical objects in mathematics, with deep ideas from modern arithmetic geometry and the theory of modular forms.

The partition function \(p(n)\) counts the number of ways a positive integer \(n\) can be written as a sum of positive integers, without regard to order. For example, \(p(4)=5\), since
\[
4,\quad 3+1,\quad 2+2,\quad 2+1+1,\quad 1+1+1+1
\]
are the five partitions of 4.

For many years, mathematicians have studied congruences and formulas for \(p(n)\). Ramanujan famously discovered remarkable congruences such as
\[
p(5n+4)\equiv 0 \pmod{5},
\]
\[
p(7n+5)\equiv 0 \pmod{7},
\]
and
\[
p(11n+6)\equiv 0 \pmod{11}.
\]
These discoveries suggested that the partition function has hidden modular properties.

Bruinier and Ono advanced this area by giving a finite algebraic formula for partition numbers. Their work showed that values of the partition function can be expressed using traces of singular moduli, which are special values of modular functions at imaginary quadratic points. This was a striking development because it linked a simple counting function to sophisticated structures in the theory of modular forms.

Their results also reflect a broader theme in modern number theory: objects that appear elementary often have deep connections to complex analysis, algebraic geometry, and automorphic forms. The work of Bruinier and Ono demonstrates how classical questions inspired by Ramanujan continue to lead to new discoveries and powerful mathematical techniques.

In this sense, the recent achievements of Bruinier and Ono not only provide new formulas and insights into partitions, but also highlight the continuing importance of modular forms in contemporary mathematics.

counterfactuals.output:
We extend the classification of Bruinier and Ono for half-integral weight cusp forms modulo odd primes to a broader class of modular forms obtained through Rankin–Cohen brackets.  For an odd prime \(\ell\), we establish criteria under which half-integral weight cusp forms modulo \(\ell\) lie in explicitly described spaces determined by congruence conditions on their Fourier coefficients and by the mod \(\ell\) behavior of associated integral weight forms.  Our method combines the algebraic properties of Rankin–Cohen brackets with filtration arguments and the theory of modular forms modulo primes, yielding a systematic mechanism for producing and detecting congruences in half-integral weight.

As applications, we derive new congruences for generating functions arising in arithmetic and combinatorics.  In particular, we obtain congruence results for traces of singular moduli, Hurwitz class numbers, and the overpartition function, showing that their associated half-integral weight modular forms fit naturally into the extended classification.  These examples illustrate how Rankin–Cohen bracket constructions provide a unified framework for explaining congruence phenomena previously observed in disparate settings, and they yield new families of congruences modulo odd primes.

\[
f(q)\in S_{\lambda+1/2}(\Gamma_0(N),\chi)\cap \mathbb Z[[q]]
\]
be a cusp form of half-integral weight, level \(N\), and Nebentypus character \(\chi\).  Using Rankin–Cohen brackets, we construct a family of modular forms of explicitly determined integral weights, levels, and characters whose Fourier coefficients encode arithmetic information about \(f\). As an application, we obtain a generalized criterion ensuring the existence of infinitely many Fourier coefficients of \(f\) satisfying prescribed congruence conditions modulo powers of primes.  Our results recover the original Bruinier–Ono theorem as the case of the zeroth Rankin–Cohen bracket and provide a systematic method for producing higher-order analogues.  The methods combine the algebraic properties of Rankin–Cohen operators, Sturm-type bounds, and the theory of half-integral weight modular forms.
